newsitem.title: USA: CME nearby hogs end lower on weaker cash hog ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME nearby hogs end lower on weaker cash hog ideas.

text.p: Expectations of steady to weak cash hog prices through the long holiday weekend period kept nearby CME hog futures pressured at the close Thursday. However, back months ended higher on spread rolling and spillover from higher pork belly futures, traders said.
Hogs finished 0.575 cent per lb lower to 0.400 higher with limitless February off most at 73.750 cents and April off 0.025 at 74.400 cents. June paced the gain in deferreds.
Pork belly futures ended 1.100 to 0.050 cent per lb higher with February up most at 79.000 cents and active March finished up the least at 78.575 cents.

Continued weakness in cash pork products prompted ideas that cash hog markets will be under pressure, especially during the long holiday period. Some packing plants will be closed for the President's Day holiday and this should keep packer bids down, traders said.
"It's still a weak tone on the product overall," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.
Skold said he anticipated a lighter weekend hog slaughter compared with last Saturday, but kills should rise again next week which will keep pork prices under pressure.
February also held a premium to the latest CME lean hog index. February goes off Friday and there are no limits the last two trading days.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.58 at $73.89 per cwt.
Refco bought April and sold February early and locals sold April late. Scattered market-on-close orders supported June with Hammer Trading a buyer there, pit sources said.
In hog options, there was continued mixed buying and selling of the February 74 strike. Volatility was down in April and June, pit sources added.

Active March pork bellies traded in a wide range before ending slightly higher. Early carryover demand ran to resistance and prices tumbled for a net loss before firming again late on fund buying, traders said.

Longs kept February support following a gain in cash bellies. Posting of 100 deliveries against the February contract offered some early pressure, but traders said they still expect a strong stopper to develop based on the low number of deliverable stocks.
Cargill Investor Services bought March early and Hammer Trading bought on the rally, traders said.
Rand sold March to turn prices down before late buying by Rosenthal Collins and Cargill provided support and offset selling by R.J. O'Brien, pit sources said.
Futures will trade in normal hours on Friday but will be closed on Monday in observance of the Presidents Day holiday.
